html:
A severe drought across East Africa from mid 2011 into 2012, which turned into famine in southern Somalia. It was called the worst drought in 60 years, and about 9.5 million people in Somalia, Ethiopia, Kenya and Djibouti faced hunger.

Drought alone did not make the famine. Southern Somalia had suffered two decades of civil war, and much of it was held by al-Shabaab, an Islamist militant group that blocked many aid agencies. Western governments, trying to weaken the group, also held back aid from areas it controlled. On 20 July 2011 the United Nations declared famine in two southern regions, its first such declaration in the region in nearly thirty years.

Farmers suffered most, above all the Rahanweyn clan and the Somali Bantu minority, rather than the herders of the north. Many walked for weeks to the camps at Dadaab in Kenya and Dollo Ado in Ethiopia. A later study estimated about 258,000 deaths in Somalia, half of them children under five, most before famine was even declared.
sum: A severe drought across East Africa from mid 2011 into 2012, which turned into famine in southern Somalia. It was called the worst drought in 60 years, and about 9.5 million people in Somalia, Ethiopia, Kenya and Djibouti faced hunger.
